taste.name: Raw Editorial Grid over Boxed Product Cards
taste.trigger: When presenting product categories and new arrivals on the main storefront landing page
taste.decision: Chose 4 full-height vertical photo split columns with 0px gaps over standard padded grid cards with borders
taste.reason: Streetwear culture values high-impact lookbook editorial feel over transactional catalog listing grids

taste.name: High Contrast Pill Micro-CTA over Heavy Solid Buttons
taste.trigger: When placing key primary call-to-action buttons over complex editorial photography
taste.decision: Chose transparent pill-shaped outline buttons with 1px white borders (border-radius: 9999px) over solid filled rectangular block buttons
taste.reason: Solid buttons obstruct the underlying outfit styling photo; a slim outlined pill frames the text legibly without obscuring the lookbook photograph

taste.name: Warm Organic Cream Accent Ticker over Stark White Utility Bar
taste.trigger: When designing top announcement and notification bars for shipping/promotional messages
taste.decision: Chose a warm sand tone (#f2e8db) with dark brown typography (#1c1b18) over standard stark white (#ffffff) or generic black (#000000)
taste.reason: Pure white utility bars feel generic and industrial; warm sand tones create a vintage, tactile paper feel that sets a relaxed premium tone

taste.name: Absolute Shadow Restraint over Elevated UI Cards
taste.trigger: When layering content sections, navigation header, and interactive product containers
taste.decision: Chose flat box-shadow: none layout surfaces, using photograph contrast and typography hierarchy for depth instead of drop shadows
taste.reason: Artificial drop shadows make digital storefronts look like software dashboards; flat photographic surfaces feel like physical editorial print magazines
evidence: box-shadow: none on 100% of hero cards
